elements.element: This Agreement must be governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 states: “This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York must have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to “the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.” The injunctive-relief sentence is limited to “those courts” and therefore creates no out-of-forum exception.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York must have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to “the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.” The injunctive-relief sentence is limited to “those courts” and therefore creates no out-of-forum exception.

elements.element: The Agreement must be governed by the laws of Delaware or California, or by the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any fallback governing law.

elements.element: The chosen courts must correspond to the fallback governing law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or the courts of London for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 selects state and federal courts in New York County rather than Delaware, California, or London courts.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position by selecting New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts located in New York County. It also narrows the temporary-injunctive-relief language to those same courts, eliminating the original exception to exclusive New York venue. The changes are confined to the governing-law and forum requirements, retain the submission and waiver language, and introduce no contradiction.
